verdicts.reasoning: All items ask the student to mentally represent and convert a textual description of a partitioned shape (e.g., '3 equal parts, 5 parts shaded' in seed 42) into its corresponding mathematical fraction.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: The items lack actual visual models, forcing a text-based interpretation that is physically nonsensical for a single shape (e.g. 'A shape is divided into 4 equal parts with 9 parts shaded').

verdicts.reasoning: Every item focuses on fractions, explicitly asking 'What fraction of the shape is shaded?' and providing fractional options (e.g., 9/4, 5/3, 6/6) for the answer.

These specific seeds test fractions that are exactly equal to one, describing scenarios where the number of shaded parts matches the total equal parts (e.g., 6/6 in seeds 57 and 127, and 3/3 in seed 91).

These items present fractions with a value greater than one (improper fractions). For example, seed 11 describes 9 parts shaded for 4 equal parts (9/4), and seed 42 describes 5 parts shaded for 3 equal parts (5/3).

There are no visual models rendered in any of the items. Instead, they rely entirely on textual descriptions (e.g., 'A shape is divided into...'), which fails to fulfill the requirement to use actual models.
verdicts.action_taken: Filed as a §6F CONTRADICTED finding, unedited. Word problems use purely textual story descriptions without drawing visual bar/group models.
